items.title: National Respite Resource Center
items.description: The ARCH National Respite Resource Center (funded by the U.S. Administration for Community Living) is the national clearinghouse for respite care information, including a respite locator tool and a provider directory.
items.use: Finding local respite providers, learning about respite funding, and accessing toolkits for families.

items.title: National Respite Network
items.description: A membership association of respite providers and advocates working to expand respite services nationwide.
items.use: Connecting with state respite coalitions and learning about respite policy and training.

items.title: Family Caregiver Alliance (FCA)
items.description: A national nonprofit with educational resources for caregivers and a directory of caregiver support programs by state.
items.use: State-by-state caregiver resource guides and educational fact sheets on respite and caregiving strategies.

items.title: Caregiver Action Network (CAN)
items.description: A national nonprofit providing free educational resources and a family caregiver helpline.
items.use: Caregiver helpline (877-CAREGIVER), educational guides, and finding local support.

items.title: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — Caregiver Support Program
items.description: For veterans and post-9/11 veterans, the VA offers respite care through the Caregiver Support Program, including in-home respite and temporary residential respite.
items.use: Eligibility information, respite care details, and applying for VA caregiver support.

items.title: Eldercare Locator
items.description: A service of the U.S. Administration for Community Living that connects older adults and their families to local services, including respite care.

items.title: Family Caregiver Alliance (FCA) — Caregiver Online
items.description: FCA offers online support communities and educational webinars for family caregivers.
items.use: Joining online caregiver communities and accessing free caregiver education.

items.title: Caregiver Action Network (CAN) — Support & Helpline
items.description: CAN runs a free national helpline (877-CAREGIVER) and connects caregivers to support resources.
items.use: Calling or chatting with trained staff for support and guidance.

items.title: Alzheimer's Association
items.description: A national nonprofit offering 24/7 helpline, online support communities, and in-person support groups for Alzheimer's and dementia caregivers.
items.use: 24/7 helpline (800-272-3900), online support groups, and local chapter information.

items.title: National Alliance for Caregiving
items.description: A national coalition that researches caregiving and partners with organizations to support family caregivers.
items.use: Research, reports, and connecting to partner caregiver programs.

items.title: Caregiver Action Network — Caregiver Online Library
items.description: A free library of caregiver guides organized by condition and situation.
items.use: Downloading free guides on specific caregiving topics.

items.title: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — Caregiver Support Program
items.description: The VA offers peer support mentoring and monthly support groups for family caregivers of veterans.

items.title: Medicare.gov
items.description: The official U.S. Medicare website, with guides to coverage, costs, and plans.
items.use: Understanding Medicare coverage for home health care and durable medical equipment.

items.title: Medicaid.gov
items.description: The official U.S. Medicaid website, with state-by-state program information.
items.use: Learning about Medicaid long-term care and home- and community-based services.

items.title: Social Security Administration (SSA)
items.description: The official SSA site, with information on Social Security, SSI, and benefits for caregivers and dependents.
items.use: Applying for or managing Social Security and SSI benefits.

items.title: Eldercare Locator
items.description: A service of the U.S. Administration for Community Living that connects people to local benefits and services.
items.use: Finding local benefit programs and financial assistance by ZIP code.

items.title: Benefits.gov
items.description: The official U.S. government benefits portal, listing federal, state, and local benefit programs.
items.use: Searching for federal benefits by life event, including caregiving-related assistance.

items.title: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — Benefits
items.description: The official VA site for veterans benefits, including disability compensation, pension, and dependent benefits.
items.use: Understanding veterans benefits that may support family caregivers.

items.title: 211.org (United Way)
items.description: United Way's 211 service connects people to local health and human services, including utility and rent assistance.

items.title: Legal Services Corporation (LSC)
items.description: The nonprofit corporation established by Congress to support civil legal aid for low-income Americans. LSC funds state legal aid organizations.
items.use: Finding your state's legal aid organization through LSC's online directory.

items.title: National Legal Aid & Defender Association (NLADA)
items.description: The oldest and largest national organization dedicated to equal justice for low-income Americans.
items.use: Connecting to legal aid programs and learning about civil legal aid.

items.title: AARP Legal Services
items.description: AARP offers legal services for members, including help with powers of attorney, advance directives, and caregiving-related documents.
items.use: Understanding legal document options and connecting to legal help.

items.title: National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA)
items.description: A national professional association of attorneys specializing in elder law.
items.use: Finding an elder law attorney through NAELA's attorney directory.

items.title: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — Veterans Benefits Administration
items.description: The official VA site for veterans benefits and appeals.
items.use: Understanding veterans benefits and filing appeals.

items.title: Medicare.gov — Appeals
items.description: The official Medicare site with information on appealing coverage and payment decisions.
